reviews.text: I’ve been coming here for years and before it was for my own pets it was for my in-laws exotic pets. David is always so nice and so very helpful. I wanted to drop a positive review because upon reading some others I wanted to assure future customers that this place knows their stuff! They treat EVERYONE with respect and give plenty of knowledge. They do tend to get a bit busy here and there, so if you want information or one on one time with an associate come with a bit of patience and understanding. They will give you the help and knowledge you seek!

I'm appalled by the way the animals are being kept here. I've never seen so many small pets being crammed into tight, and often incorrect, enclosures. Two full grown guinea pigs being kept in a glass fish tank, with no places to hide, and almost no grass for grazing is unacceptable. The birds were equally lacking in space or correct cage care. Many of these animals been to be kept in wide cages to regulate air temperature as they are prone to illness. I saw quite a few animals displaying signs of illness or stress, such as missing patches of hair or feathers. I would not buy a pet from here, and am deeply upset to see how these animals are living.
The living conditions of the smaller animals (rats, hamsters, etc) are inhumane. I could not stand one minute in this place.

I love gerbils like it is a religion, and Jules is always where I go for my gerbs. Their gerbils are well handled and friendly.

I always recommend gerbils as a first low maintenance pocket pet for people with kids. They are curiousity not food motivated, so if they get out they don't hide they just explore and are easy to catch again. They generally don't bite (though individual gerbils may taste you I have had nippers over the years). They are from the desert so their pee is concentrated and doesn't smell much, and you should give them a sand toilet. Super charming to watch, but diurnal so better in the living room than the bedroom because they are awake and asleep during the day and the night. Their nails are sharp, so dress kids in long sleeves to hold so they aren't too tickly. They are social so get at least 2, and if they have babies leave the dad in because gerbil dads parent well and help keep mom from getting too stressed. Seriously best pet.

I don’t leave bad reviews almost ever. But I have to here.

A few weeks ago, my boyfriend decided to gift my cockatiel a new cage. And I am so grateful to him. So is my Ziggy bird. I am a lucky girl.

We thought we got a good deal on the used cage they gave us, but as soon as we got home, I found a price tag on the cage that was like $20 cheaper than what we paid. He got ripped off. Thats not even the reason for this review.

A week or so after the cage came home, I was horrified to find a roach in the kitchen. I want to emphasize that before that day, I had NEVER seen a roach in the apartment. I did the right thing, contacted the landlord and put bait out and sprayed. I lived in a roach infested apartment YEARS ago so I knew what to do immediately.

There were suddenly several more roach sightings after having never had an issue in this apartment before. It was clear the roaches came from somewhere and it wasn’t just a few crawling in from outside.

After I put the bait out, I started seeing dead baby roaches around the cage and realized with dread that they hitched a ride in the holes of the cage.

We just confirmed this suspicion today by hosing out the holes in the stand. Several roaches came out and there are still dead ones inside. I am enclosing a picture. Idk if it is super apparent from my photography skills but it’s clear the cage was infested.

There is no way the roaches became so concentrated in the cage after the cage got here. That’s not how roaches work. If that were the case, we would have seen roaches in the apartment before the cage got home. The cage is the only explanation and I wasn’t even 100% sure until today. I did not write this review until I was 100% sure.

Had I not known what to do from years before, this apartment would now have an infestation. I don’t write this review lightly. Having had a roach infestation years ago, I know how embarrassing it is. Plus this is a small, local business. But this is a business selling cages that can bring roaches to unsuspecting customers so I have to write something. They need to do in depth pest control.

Update: We now have a roach infestation in our apartment due to the cage

Two ferrets in a cage with zero beds, birds in cages so small they cannot open their wings, none of the cages were clean. They had multiple bearded dragons housed together. Seems like it should be illegal to house animals in these conditions...

TAKE BETTER CARE OF YOUR ANIMALS. Deplorable conditions for the animals. Feed them. Change their water. Give animals heat lamps that need it. Treat the mite problem. Should be shut down for the abuse caused to animals here.

I genuinely dislike leaving reviews like this for small buisness, but animals are living creatures and deserve to have their basic needs met.

This pet shop needs to reevaluate its animal welfare standards. Before I had even stepped fully inside I was met with a pungent smell of ammonia. The pervasive ammonia odor came from nearly every cage.

The reptiles lacked proper enclosures per their species. The bird husbandry in general is lacking at most pet stores, however, this store somehow managed to make it worse. There were cages next to each other where the birds in both cages were trying repeatedly to attack each other-- this went on for the entirety of my visit. There were quite a few birds being kept in small-shallow enclosures with the only opening for air circulation being on the top. This might not be an issue except for the stagnant stale air around the enclosures accompanied by the smell of feces coming from within. I'm not surprised they don't offer returns (warranties) with their birds.

The mammals were in the best situations of the non-aquatic animals. But still lacked proper enclosures, notably one hamster being in a plastic cage with nothing but a cup of food.

The fish seemed to be well cared for.

Overall, I would avoid purchasing anything here. Even if you're able to overlook all the bad animal husbandry, the entire interior was dirty. Not just the kind of dirty that comes from housing many animals, but the kind that indicates a lack of care for cleanliness. Debris in corners, walkways, and on every shelf.  The whole inside needed swept, and wiped down.

This was overall a sad store to experience. I'd be happy to do a return visit and adjust my review if conditions improve.
The reptile enclosures are incredibly small. I feel terrible for those snakes and bearded dragons. Many of the bird enclosures seemed very cramped as well.

Jule’s Pet Shop is easily one of the best local spots I’ve visited in a long time. The owner is incredibly friendly, honest, and clearly passionate about what they do—hardworking and knowledgeable in a way that really stands out. For the shop’s size, the stock is amazing! The species selection, quality of the animals, and even the variety of aquatic plants are all impressive. You can tell the fish are well cared for and the tanks are maintained with love and attention.

I’m a frequent local shopper, but after chatting with the manager during my last visit, I’ll definitely be coming back more often. I picked up a couple of beautiful small plants for my 60-gallon tank, and my girlfriend absolutely fell in love with the two massive Oscars they had—seriously, those fish have personality! If I had the space, I would’ve taken them home on the spot. They were not only stunning, but very reasonably priced.

If you’re even slightly into aquariums or pets in general, do yourself a favor and stop by. It might just make your day like it did mine.

From my firsthand experience, DO NOT TRUST THE BIRD BREEDERS here, nor the vet or “vet.” I acquired a bird here who will be chronically ill for the rest of her life, according to FOUR different professionals whom I’ve met with - spending thousands of dollars within the first few months of this bird’s life. She has suffered emotionally and physically and I was initially told to put her down. When I first got her, the breeder here gave me a “deal.” The “vet” there told me to put coffee grounds in her eye, yet when I did research on it, multiple sites advised very strongly against that. After extensive medication, emotional support and bonding for her, I was told, although this type of bird typically lives 15-20 years, she will probably only live 5 or so. It’s caused me immense stress and seems pretty damn inhumane. Photos of her chronic/lifelong injury included.

DO NOT BUY AQUATIC PLANTS HERE. They are absolutely infested with scuds and snails. The scuds will take over your tank and are extremely difficult to get rid of. I hate to give this place a negative review because they're nice people but their plants nearly ruined my tank. To this day I still have to suck out tens if not hundreds of them a week.

Update: Had to completely nuke both of my tanks to get rid of all the scuds I got from their plants. To fellow aquarium keepers, always soak your plants in plain soda water before adding them to your tank! It will suffocate any hitchhikers without harming your plants.

As we pulled up we saw the lights turn off and I thought to myself that we didn't make it on time. I called the place and asked the gentleman on the phone if they were closed. He asked if we were nearby and I told him that we just pulled up, but saw the lights turn off. He stayed open a little longer, so that he could accommodate us. We definitely appreciate that!

He earned all future pet related business from us. I'm happy to make the trip from Schaumburg in the future.

THEY WENT AGAINST AGREEMENT AND SOLD MY GUINAE PIG OUT FROM UNDER ME AFTER I MADE A DEPOSIT AND HAD A RECEIPT. NO CALL. I’m honestly very sad about it…
I am not usually the person to write reviews but I feel the need to let folks know about my experience there and why I will not be coming back. On a Wednesday I went into Jules Pet Shop looking for Guinea pigs. I really bonded with one specific Guinea Pig and just loved her tbh. I didn’t have a cage set up yet so I didn’t feel it was responsible to bring her home just yet. I called the next day and asked if I could purchase her and have them keep her for a little bit until my cage comes in. They said they “do that all the time” and that it was “no problem” so I asked them to put a sold sign on her cage and they said they would tell the other people that work there. I went to Jules Pet Shop later that day and put down a deposit and got an official receipt and everything. I checked to make sure there was a sold sign, which there was, and I held her for a little bit before I had to leave to go get her cage set up. Once I had, I came back on a Saturday thinking I was going to pick up the wonderful guinae pig I had bonded with and was so looking foreword to adopting. When I came to pick her up I noticed she wasn’t in the cage. I waited while they looked downstairs to see if they put her down there. They then called back up to the desk that they had SOLD… SOLD… my Guinea pig who I had made a full deposit for and had a copy of their receipt that had my PHONE NUMBER on it. They did not bother to even call me to ask if I still wanted her. I left distraught and I’m really sad about it still. I think they were just going to take my money and sell her to someone else assuming I would just forget??? I certainly will never come back. To me it shows how much they care about both me, as the patron, and the animal. My feelings are hurt and I’m not even trying to be dramatic. I just wish I had my Guinea pig I had bonded with and PAID for.
